exposure: KCNJ1 gene defect (homozygous missense mutation c.212C>T, p.T71M)
cohort: The participants are a child who presented with a hypocalcemic seizure at 2.3 years of age and six additional family members diagnosed clinically with Type 2 Bartter Syndrome.
finding: The study identified a previously described homozygous missense mutation (c.212C>T, p.T71M) in the KCNJ1 gene associated with Type 2 Bartter Syndrome, expanding its clinical spectrum and highlighting the hazardous effects of phosphate-containing soft drinks on calcium metabolism.
